content:
**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant part**: Single sugarcane leaf (long, narrow, parallel venation)
- **Color pattern**: Broad, diffuse yellowing/straw-golden coloration over most of the blade; orange-brown scorching along margins and at the tip (right side); the midrib/center retains some residual green
- **Texture/pattern**: Uniform discoloration — no discrete spots, no mosaic interleaving, no twisting or distortion
- **Severity**: Advanced — most of the blade is chlorotic/necrotic

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Brown_Spot**: Discrete brown lesions with halos — not present here
- **Grassy_Shoot**: Multiple thin shoots — not a color symptom on a single leaf
- **Sett_Rot**: Affects underground setts — not applicable
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Apical twisting and distortion — no distortion here
- **Streak_Mosaic / Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Alternating green/yellow streak or mosaic pattern — no interleaved streaks visible
- **Yellow_Spot**: Discrete pale-yellow spots — not discrete spots here
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Midrib turns bright yellow (most diagnostic feature); in this image the midrib appears greener than the blade — opposite of classic Yellow Leaf presentation
- **Leaf_Scald** *(best match)*: Caused by *Xanthomonas albilineans*; in advanced stages produces the characteristic straw-yellow to orange-brown scalded appearance across the blade with reddish-brown margin necrosis, while the midrib can retain more green — matches this leaf closely

{"prediction": "Leaf_Scald", "confidence": 0.62, "reasoning": "The sugarcane leaf shows a broad, uniform straw-yellow to golden coloration with orange-brown necrotic margins and tip, while the midrib retains residual green. This scorched/scalded pattern without discrete spots, mosaic streaks, or structural distortion is most consistent with advanced Leaf Scald (Xanthomonas albilineans), where the blade becomes straw-colored and margins turn orange-brown in later disease stages."}
